**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Gold, silver and platinum all weakened in price terms during December as investors showed little appetite to build long positions in any of these metals. Palladium outperformed the other three metals with investors showing continued faith in a metal which everyone agrees is eventually due to increase in value. For the entire year, gold was the only one of these four metals to see its price appreciate. The outlook for the prices of all four metals are somewhat mixed: while we see reasons to be bullish for the precious metal complex, the pronounced price weakness which has been seen since September demonstrates the continuing concerns over economic growth and the health of the Euro. • There were decreases in net long speculative positioning for all four of the major precious metals in the final week of 2011. More importantly, investor exposure remains low by recent standards for all of the metals and any moves higher could drive some renewed buying interest. Expect the first few days of 2012 to set the tone for the first quarter of the year. • 2011 was a mixed year for ETF flows with gold and platinum seeing net inflows of metal from investors and silver and palladium experiencing substantial net outflows, in contrast to the previous year’s heavy buying. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **03 January 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **03 January 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 27 December 2011; ETF data to 30 December 2011.** ### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

The impending introduction of a rule forcing the reporting of sales of precious metal in excess of 2 million Yen to the Japanese tax authorities drove substantial selling of gold by the general public in Japan and forced the price lower in thin trading. Gold slipped below $1,600 on the 26th and crashed to a low of $1,525 on the 29th as the Euro weakened against the Dollar. Gold has since regained some energy to challenge the $1,600 level again. Looking at last year in total, gold gained roughly $140. For those who prefer their glass half empty, though, gold lost over $400 from its intra-year high. - Net long speculative gold positions on COMEX fell by 400,000 ounces to 17 million ounces in the week to the 27th of December. This is their lowest level since April 2009. To a large extent, this reflects the growing gloom in the gold market following recent falls in the metal price. However, with much of the market remaining bullish over the medium term, this low long positioning could allow gold to gain some ground in price terms. - Global Exchange Traded Fund holdings of gold climbed by only 2.8 million ounces during 2011 despite heightened concerns over slowing economic growth and sovereign debt worries in Europe. This relatively low level of buying could suggest that risk fatigue has set in with further economic concerns unlikely to drive as much gold buying as before. At the end of the year, they totalled 69.2 million ounces. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—December 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Silver ended 2011 surprisingly weakly. It briefly regained the $30 per ounce level on the 21st but investors did not show any great interest and the silver price softened to just above $29 ahead of Christmas. As the market returned, silver accompanied gold downwards with the Euro’s weakness forcing silver as low as $26.30 on the 29th before it recovered some ground. Looking upwards, the short term targets for the silver price lie near $30. However, the price trend has been resoundingly negative since late August, so further downwards pressure might be expected. - Net long speculative positions in silver on COMEX fell by a further 5.8 million ounces to 92.7 million ounces in the week to the 27th of December. Positioning has not been this low since 2003, demonstrating the impact of high levels of price volatility on the willingness of investors to hold positions. Although the short term prospects for the silver price are not entirely positive, there is certainly scope for increased investor appetite to drive prices higher once again. - Silver ETF flows were interesting in the final third of 2011. Even as the silver price fell by a third from its late August highs, total global ETF holdings stayed close to 450 million ounces, ending the year just below 454 million ounces. For the entire year, net outflows were

33.6 million ounces, rather than the net buying of 90 million ounces seen in 2010. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **03 January 2012** ## **Platinum CFTC data to 27 December 2011; ETF data to 30 December 2011.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

- From the middle of December, the platinum price finally found some stability above the $1,400 level. The price firmed to $1,440 and then settled in a narrow range around $1,430 until the 28th. A sudden spell of Euro weakness sent platinum tumbling to $1,350 on the 29th, testing investors’ resolve once again. Fortunately, the euro turned around again that day and platinum bounced to end the year close to $1,400. - Net long speculative positions in platinum on NYMEX fell for the third successive week leading up to the 27th of December, dropping by 22,000 ounces to 1.07 million ounces. Although this is a third lower than the level of speculative interest in platinum at the start of September before the price fell, investors seem to remain relatively bullish. - At the end of December 2011, platinum ETF holdings were 1.40 million ounces. This was broadly unchanged during December but an increase of 140,000 ounces from the start of the year. However, Q4 saw selling pressure intensifying as the platinum price fell. Positive price action now could support a return to ETF buying. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and

- December was a positive month for the palladium price which climbed from an opening $615 to a closing $655. Of the four major precious metals, palladium was the only one to gain ground in price terms. The end of the month was no different: while the other metals weakened slowly, palladium found buying interest, challenging $660 again on the 23rd and 27th before falling back as the Dollar firmed against the Euro. Even at this point, though, palladium remained relatively robust, dropping only as far as $630 before bouncing back to a first fix for 2012 of $655. - Net long speculative interest in palladium increased by a trivial 7,100 ounces on NYMEX to 586,000 ounces in the final full week of 2011. This remains less than a third of the highest level of interest seen during 2011. Any upward movement in the palladium price could drive buying and reinforce the sense that the longer term bullish trend could yet become reality. - At the end of 2011, palladium ETF holdings stood at 1.736 million ounces. Net selling of palladium throughout the year was 530,000 ounces, a stark change from the 1.1 million ounces of net buying which took place in 2010. The selling pressure has continued in recent weeks and early 2012 could see investors’ optimism tested further. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals
